correctness.rationale: The exact metric identity in antipodal ellipse angle coordinates and the exact arclength density determine the distribution. There are exactly two isolated quadratic maximum neighborhoods at fixed positive eccentricity; local scaling yields coefficient 4πb²/(aP²sqrtδ). The circle event has a directly measurable angular length. In double scaling δ/(ε/a)->λ finite, a bounded rescaled v-domain permits dominated convergence, giving the stated positive-part square-root angular integral. Complete elliptic substitution and classical DLMF §19.12 endpoint series yield the exact two-branch profile and logarithmic cusp. All constants and domains were checked independently with 15 numerical quadratures against exact integrals. Numeric checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The near-diametral single-pair boundary distance law changes asymptotic exponent from one to one-half in the circle limit. This theorem identifies the noncommuting limits, the exact universal double-scaling profile, and the nonanalytic logarithmic threshold at normalized eccentricity one. The finding quantifies a meaningful geometric endpoint degeneracy and is neither an arbitrary slice nor a restatement of circle-distance or classical elliptic-integral formulas.
